recipes.name: Roasted Potato Medley
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup low fat, low sodium chicken broth

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a mixing bowl, combine the russet potato, red potato, sweet potato, olive oil, vinegar, thyme, garlic and chicken broth. Toss well to coat.
Place into casserole dish and roast uncovered for 40 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Potato Medley
raw_recipe.description: Russet, red and sweet potatoes are roasted with olive oil, garlic and balsamic vinegar in this tasty low-fat side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Roasted Potato Medley

review.reviewBody: Super easy, delicious, nice presentation, and healthful--what more could you ask! I used Yukon Gold and sweet potatoes, and I followed the advice of other reviewers, decreasing balsamic vinegar to 1 1/2 Tbsp. and increasing chicken broth to 3/4 cup. I also used 1/2 tsp. of dried thyme because I didn't have fresh. I baked for one hour, stirring 2 or 3 times during baking to ensure that none of the pieces on top dried out. It turned out great. Even my five-year-old, who generally dislikes sweet potatoes, loved them in this dish. I can't wait to make it again.

This was bomb! I had it with thin sliced turkey breast and broccoli tonight and it was a hit! I listened to others and put sweet potatoes and red potatoes and added more chicken broth. I also cooked them for an hour while tossing them midway. I used balsamic vinaigrette salad dressing because that’s what I had. I also added some oregano. The garlic powder and dried thyme leaves worked just fine as well! Thank you thank you !..... THANK YOU!

I took the advice of some reviewers and put in a cup of chicken broth, cut back slightly on the vinegar and doubled the baking time. I also added the thyme and garlic near the end of the cooking time, so they wouldn't get overdone. This also definitely needs salt, plus I sprinkled with freshly ground pepper and paprika. It was very tasty, but I found myself really liking the sweet potatoes so much better than the other types of potatoes in the dish. I think I'll make this again, but only with sweet potatoes. With these changes, I would rate this more like four or five stars.

I've made these twice - and I kind of just throw together any potatoes I have (I love adding purple potatoes for color!). Delicious both times, but I cook them on a baking sheet on aluminum foil, not in a casserole dish. When I pull them out of the oven, I wrap up the foil around the potatoes to keep them cooking/warm, and when I'm ready to serve they slide off the foil very easily.
Upped the chicken broth to 1 cup. Baked for an hour. Used red and sweet potatoes only and used tarragon and parsley, delicious!

Wow! Who knew that sweet potatoes taste so good with balsamic vinegar! I had half a baked sweet potato and half a baked Idaho potato leftover, so I cubed them and tossed them in 1/3 the seasonings, let them sit 10 minutes to soak up the vinegar and oil, then heated them for a minute or 2 in the microwave. I used granular boullion instead of liquid stock and garlic powder instead of fresh. Delicious!

This was pretty good. I thought it was a much healthier alternative to the way I used to make them. My husband and company really enjoyed. I reduced the vinegar by a little, but I think I will reduce by half the next time and will probably enjoy them more. TO REDUCE BAKING TIME - I pre-boil the potatoes to close to be tender (before they begin to fall apart)then pop them in the oven - still baked for 40+ minutes without ever getting them crusty like I like 'em. Next time I'll put them under the broiler for a few minutes.

I dropped the temperature to 350 since it was going into the oven with a meatloaf and baked for a little over an hour. I used only the garlic and salt and pepper since I didn't have the fresh herbs on hand and omitted the broth. It was very good!

I don't usually care for sweet potatoes, but I really enjoyed this dish and will make it again. I made a few adjustments due to what was in my pantry: I only used sweet potatoes, 1/2 tsp dried thyme instead of fresh, no balsamic, and substituted 3/4 cup of vegetable broth instead of chicken to keep it vegan. Baked for approximately 50 minutes and flipped/stirred the potatoes around every 15 minutes-isn.

I cut the potatoes pretty small, probably a 1/2 inch cube, and they cooked quickly compared to the other reviews. I omitted the vinegar and the chicken broth, but added chicken bouillon powder as a salt element, tossed everything in a bowl to coat, and baked in a glass dish greased with more olive oil. I stirred them twice during baking, and in the end had crispy, tasty potatoes. I will make this again with my changes.

This did nothing for me. The sweet potatoes cooked much faster than the white potatoes and the seasoning was bland. I would at least double the thyme and omit the broth completely and just roast on a baking sheet. I had to cook much longer to get the russet potatoes at an edible consistency and even still I had to nuke it.
Omitted vinegar and added onion - I’ll make it again!
Taste yummy. I only used chicken broth, dried minced garlic, and zesty garlic herbs but i followed the directions of this recipe and it turned out great.
Delicious...I did add more chicken broth as some suggested.
Easy to make, I really liked it, my picky children said it tasted funny, probably because the sweet potatoes were not drenched in butter, brown sugar and marshmallows.

I make a double recipe of these potatoes for Christmas every year, and they are a huge hit. 

The only change I make is that I use Yukon Gold instead of russet. It is a pretty dish and delicious dish.
I enjoyed these roasted potatoes. My only disappointment is the timing it was way off.
Tastes great but cooking time is WAY off. 425 for 40-45 mins is much better.
Loved this--the balsamic vinegar gives it a nice flavor. I didn't have any red potatoes, but used a mixture of white and sweet.
